prompt: You are now from Alabama. Someone at a conference made assumptions. You may mention football exactly once. Defend your state with your whole chest.
response:
Excuse me, I couldn't help but overhear your little joke a minute ago. It's funny how folks travel to these professional conferences, look at the "AL" on my nametag, and immediately let their tired, lazy stereotypes do the talking. Let me educate you for a second, since you clearly think we're just a bunch of barefoot folks living in the past. 

Did you use GPS today? Do you appreciate the fact that humanity has walked on the moon? You can thank Huntsville, Alabama, for that. The Saturn V rocket was designed in our backyard. The Rocket City has one of the highest concentrations of engineers and aerospace professionals in the entire country. We don't just look up at the future; we literally build the vehicles that take us there.

Let’s talk about innovation. UAB down in Birmingham is conducting world-class, groundbreaking medical research and clinical trials that are saving lives across the globe right this very second. We manufacture the cars you drive—from Mercedes to Honda. 

Let’s talk about culture. The greatest musicians of the 20th century—Aretha Franklin, The Rolling Stones, Etta James—flocked to the swamps of Muscle Shoals, Alabama, because we had the absolute best sound and session players in the world. And let’s not forget that the profound courage that changed the fabric of this nation's equality was born, bled for, and realized on the streets of Montgomery, Birmingham, and Selma. 

Look, I get it. It’s real easy to punch down based on some exhausted television trope. Yes, we take immense pride in our college football, but if you think that's the only thing we have going for us, you are just being willfully ignorant. 

Alabama is aerospace. It is life-saving science. It is deep musical soul. It is literary titans, civil rights giants, and unparalleled natural beauty stretching from the Appalachian foothills straight down to the sugar-white sands of the Gulf Coast. 

So the next time you decide to run your mouth about my home state over bad convention center coffee, I strongly suggest you check your facts first. We belong in every room we walk into. Have a great rest of your conference.
